title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Typical Cases of People's Courts Protecting Consumer Rights
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Release of Typical Cases on Consumer Rights Protection by People's Courts

Case 1

Meng Jian v. Guangzhou Jianmin Pharmaceutical Chain Co., Ltd., Hainan Yangshengtang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., and Hangzhou Yangshengtang Health Products Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Product Liability

— Health Food Illegally Using Additives Is Unsafe Food; Consumers Have the Right to Claim Ten Times the Purchase Price as Compensation

(1) Basic Facts

On July 27 and 28, 2012, Meng Jian purchased a total of 7 boxes of "Yangshengtang Collagen Powder" (produced by Hangzhou Yangshengtang Health Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Hangzhou Yangshengtang Company") and supervised by Hainan Yangshengtang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Hainan Yangshengtang Company")) from Guangzhou Jianmin Pharmaceutical Chain Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Jianmin Company"), for a total of RMB 1,736. The production dates were September 28, 2011 and November 5, 2011, respectively. The outer packaging of the products indicated the product standard number: Q/YST0011S, and the ingredients included "food additives (D-mannitol, citric acid)". All parties confirmed that the products in question were ordinary food and contained the food additive D-mannitol, which constituted an abuse of food additives beyond the permitted scope and did not meet the national food safety standards. After failing to obtain compensation from the food operator, Meng Jian filed a lawsuit with the Yuexiu District People's Court of Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province, requesting that Hainan Yangshengtang Company, Hangzhou Yangshengtang Company, and Jianmin Company refund the purchase price of RMB 1,736 and pay ten times the purchase price as compensation, i.e., RMB 17,360.

(2) Judgment

The court of first instance ruled that Hangzhou Yangshengtang Company should refund Meng Jian the purchase price of RMB 1,736, and Hainan Yangshengtang Company should bear joint and several liability for the above amount. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Meng Jian appealed to the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court.

The court of second instance held that: First, the focus of the dispute in this case was whether the addition of D-mannitol to the products in question complied with the provisions of the food safety standards. The products in question were solid beverages, not candies, and the permitted use of D-mannitol was limited to candies. Therefore, in accordance with the regulations on the use of food additives, the addition of D-mannitol to the products by Yangshengtang Company did not meet the provisions of the food safety standards. The evidence provided by Hangzhou Yangshengtang Company could not support its claim. Second, regarding whether Article 96 of the Food Safety Law regarding ten times compensation was applicable in this case. In this case, since the addition of D-mannitol to the products in question did not meet the food safety standards, consumers could, in accordance with that provision, demand from the producer or seller compensation of ten times the purchase price. In the second instance, Meng Jian clearly stated that he only required Hainan Yangshengtang Company and Hangzhou Yangshengtang Company to bear liability, and Hainan Yangshengtang Company and Hangzhou Yangshengtang Company should pay Meng Jian compensation of ten times the purchase price of the products in question. The court of second instance ruled that Hangzhou Yangshengtang Company should pay Meng Jian compensation of RMB 17,360, and Hainan Yangshengtang Company should bear joint and several liability for this amount.

Case 2

Zhao Xiaohong v. Beijing Fanmei Zhuoyue Furniture Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Sales Contract

— Selling Furniture Made of Board and Wood as Solid Wood Furniture Constitutes Commercial Fraud; the Seller Shall Bear Liability of "Return the Goods and Pay One Time the Purchase Price as Compensation"

(1) Basic Facts

On October 1, 2010, Zhao Xiaohong purchased several pieces of furniture from Beijing Fanmei Zhuoyue Furniture Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Fanmei Company") for a total price of RMB 23,960. The furniture in question bore markings such as "birch", "American red birch", "walnut", etc., and the furniture delivery note additionally indicated that the furniture was "solid wood". Later, Zhao Xiaohong discovered that the furniture in question was actually made of a combination of board and wood, and thus filed a lawsuit with the Chaoyang District People's Court of Beijing, requesting the return of the furniture in question and the purchase price, as well as compensation of RMB 23,960.

Fanmei Company admitted that some of the products in question had quality defects, but denied that they constituted product quality problems, and claimed that it had informed Zhao Xiaohong during the sales process that the products in question were made of board and wood. However, Fanmei Company could not provide purchase vouchers, invoices, product certificates, manuals, etc., for the furniture in question.

(2) Judgment

The court of first instance held that the evidence provided by Fanmei Company was insufficient to prove the true information and quality of the furniture in question, and it should bear the corresponding product quality liability. At the same time, considering the markings on the delivery note and the textual descriptions of the products in Fanmei Company's promotional images, which were all expressed as "XX wood" or "solid wood", the furniture company had engaged in misleading false publicity, constituting fraud against Zhao Xiaohong. Therefore, the court ruled in favor of Zhao Xiaohong's claims. Fanmei Company appealed to the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court. On November 20, 2012, the court of second instance upheld the original judgment.

Case 3

Wang Weiwen v. Sun Yuncai — Dispute over Sales Contract

— Where a Seller Promises "Compensate Ten Times for Counterfeit Goods" and the Sold Goods Are Counterfeit, the Seller Shall Comply with Its Promise

(1) Basic Facts

On October 25, 2011, Wang Weiwen purchased a Nokia mobile phone from Sun Yuncai's business premises located in a shopping mall at a price of RMB 1,180. At the same time, Sun Yuncai issued a purchase receipt to Wang Weiwen, which stated the phone model, unit price, quantity, and also indicated "guaranteed genuine, compensate ten times for counterfeits". After appraisal, Wang Weiwen learned that the phone was a counterfeit product, and thus filed a lawsuit with the Dongcheng District People's Court of Beijing, requesting that Sun Yuncai pay compensation of RMB 11,800 in accordance with the "compensate ten times for counterfeits" promise, as well as pay appraisal fees of RMB 260.

(2) Judgment

The court of first instance held that good faith is a fundamental principle stipulated in the General Principles of the Civil Law, and Sun Yuncai's promise of "compensate ten times for counterfeits" to promote sales constituted a contractual act. Wang Weiwen decided to purchase the product, the sales contract was established, and this promise, together with other terms of the contract, was legally binding on the operator. Sun Yuncai had made the promise of "compensate ten times for counterfeits" to Wang Weiwen and should perform it in accordance with the contract. Wang Weiwen's request for Sun Yuncai to pay compensation of RMB 11,800 and appraisal fees of RMB 260 was legally well-founded, so the court ruled in favor of Wang Weiwen's claims. Dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, Sun Yuncai appealed to the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court. On April 18, 2012, the court of second instance upheld the original judgment.

Case 4

Wu Hailin v. Zhu Wangqi — Dispute over Consumer Rights Protection

— Where a Seller Makes False Statements About Health Products, a Consumer Who Knowingly Buys Counterfeit Goods Has the Right to Claim "Return the Goods and Pay One Time the Purchase Price as Compensation" from the Seller

(1) Basic Facts

Chunhe Pharmacy was operated by Zhu Wangqi. Between March and August 2009, Wu Hailin purchased Guang'entang brand Huoshi Xianqing Spray (10 boxes in total) from Chunhe Pharmacy on eight separate occasions, for a total amount of RMB 3,080. The outer packaging of the product indicated that the product was produced by Lhasa Guang'entang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Guang'entang Company"), and the commissioned manufacturer was Guizhou Miaorentang Biomedical Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Miaorentang Company"). The production approval certificate for Miaoling brand Xianqing Spray (a health product, permit No. Shaanxi Food and Drug Administration Health Use 06070258) obtained by Miaorentang Company in 2006 was publicly revoked by the Shaanxi Food and Drug Administration in July 2008, and the announcement clearly stated that "continued production under the original approval document number shall be deemed illegal production". In light of this, Wu Hailin filed a lawsuit with the Chong'an District People's Court of Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province, requesting that Zhu Wangqi pay double compensation of RMB 6,160. Zhu Wangqi argued that Wu Hailin knowingly bought counterfeit goods and was not a consumer, and thus the lawsuit should be dismissed. The court of first instance dismissed Wu Hailin's claims. After Wu Hailin's appeal was rejected, he applied for retrial.

(2) Judgment

The Wuxi Intermediate People's Court held during the retrial: Operators and consumers shall conduct transactions in accordance with the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith. Operators shall provide consumers with true information about the goods or services and shall not engage in misleading false publicity. The Guang'entang brand Huoshi Xianqing Spray purchased by Wu Hailin from Chunhe Pharmacy was all produced by Miaorentang Company. Since Guang'entang Company entrusted Miaorentang Company (whose production permit had been revoked) to produce the Xianqing Spray, which was an illegal act, and the product itself involved misleading false publicity, the sale of the above product by Chunhe Pharmacy should be deemed to constitute fraudulent conduct. Accordingly, Chunhe Pharmacy should compensate the consumer for the losses suffered, with the amount of compensation being double the purchase price of the goods. In this case, Wu Hailin's request that Zhu Wangqi, the owner of Chunhe Pharmacy, pay double compensation totaling RMB 6,160 (equal to the purchase price of RMB 3,080) should be upheld. Therefore, the court ruled that Zhu Wangqi should pay Wu Hailin RMB 6,160 as compensation.

Case 5

Wang Yulan v. Wuhan Hanfu Supermarket Co., Ltd., Guanggu Branch — Dispute over Right to Reputation

— Where a Consumer Suffers No Economic Loss but Experiences Serious Mental Harm Due to Insult to Personality, the Seller Shall Bear Liability for Compensation for Mental Damage

(1) Basic Facts

On the afternoon of October 18, 2011, Wang Yulan was shopping at the Carrefour Guanggu store operated by Wuhan Hanfu Supermarket Co., Ltd., Guanggu Branch (hereinafter "Hanfu Company"). Seeing a promoter recommending a "buy five get one free" promotion for Ximai oatmeal, she purchased 20 bags. With the promoter's assistance, she packed 24 bags of oatmeal into a shopping bag. At the checkout, Wang Yulan and the cashier had a dispute over whether the four bags of oatmeal without free gift tags should be paid for. A store security guard took Wang Yulan and the selected items to the store's risk prevention office. Wang Yulan argued that the four bags of oatmeal were free gifts and did not need to be paid for. After the security guard obtained statements from two store employees that there was no oatmeal giveaway promotion, he took photos of Wang Yulan and the selected items and asked her to sign a form. Wang Yulan, who suffered from poor eyesight, signed without clearly reading the contents. Subsequently, the promoter affixed "not for sale" labels to the four bags of oatmeal and took Wang Yulan to settle the bill.

On the 19th of the same month, Wang Yulan and her husband went to the Carrefour Guanggu store to see the form she had signed. In the office, they saw a "Daily Theft Record" with Wang Yulan's name in the "Suspect Name" column, and her signature and photos of the purchased items were attached as "screenshots of the suspect." Wang Yulan demanded an apology, but the store refused. On the morning of the 20th, accompanied by her husband and a reporter from the Yangtze River Business Daily, Wang Yulan went again to the Carrefour Guanggu store. Only then did she learn that she had signed a "Security Department Report and Receipt" on the 18th. The form listed all the items she had selected as "lost goods", and the processing flow column noted "released after education." Wang Yulan pointed out that apart from her signature, all other content and fingerprints on the form were written or affixed by others, and she demanded a written apology from Hanfu Company. Because the company did not respond on the spot, Wang Yulan knelt down to demand that her reputation be cleared. Hanfu Company then handed over the "Daily Theft Record" to Wang Yulan. After mediation failed, Wang Yulan filed a lawsuit with the Wuhan Donghu New Technology Development Zone People's Court of Hubei Province, claiming that Hanfu Company had seriously infringed upon her personal dignity and damaged her reputation. She requested that Hanfu Company make a written apology to her and post an apology letter at its business premises or publish one in the media, to eliminate the adverse effects and restore her reputation; and that Hanfu Company compensate her with RMB 5,000 for mental distress.

(2) Judgment

The court hearing the case held that the personal dignity of citizens is protected by law. Hanfu Company ultimately acknowledged that the four bags of oatmeal were free gifts, yet without Wang Yulan's knowledge, it identified her conduct as theft in the form she signed, listed her in the "Suspect Name" column of the Daily Theft Record, noted "released after education", and placed the form in a location accessible to anyone entering the office. The above conduct of Hanfu Company infringed upon Wang Yulan's personal dignity, objectively caused a certain degree of reduction in Wang Yulan's social evaluation, and damaged her reputation. The court upheld Wang Yulan's claim for a written apology and posting of an apology letter at the business premises. Accordingly, the court ruled that Hanfu Company should make a written apology to Wang Yulan, post a letter of apology to Wang Yulan at its Carrefour Guanggu store, and pay Wang Yulan RMB 5,000 as compensation for mental distress.

Case 6

Bi Yongzhen v. Hou Guangzhou — Dispute over Medical Device Quality

— Where a Seller Sells Medicine Through False Publicity Causing Damage to the Consumer, Constituting Fraud, the Seller Shall Bear Liability of "Return the Goods and Pay One Time the Purchase Price as Compensation"

(1) Basic Facts

Hou Guangzhou, as the operator of a specialty store selling "German Wagner Biochip" in Anyang, Henan Province, distributed promotional leaflets about the product bearing the store's seal. Bi Yongzhen, a diabetic patient, purchased a Wagner Biochip from Hou Guangzhou's specialty store on October 7, 2006, for RMB 2,390. After wearing the product, Bi Yongzhen stopped taking his diabetes medication. In March 2007, Bi Yongzhen felt unwell and was examined at a hospital, where his blood sugar was found to have risen to 14 points. He was hospitalized for treatment on March 13, 2007, incurring medical expenses of RMB 19,167.96, of which his personal share was RMB 2,919.24. On June 22, 2007, after watching a report on the "German Wagner Biochip" using false advertising on the "Yi Ri Shuo Fa" (Legal Report) program, Bi Yongzhen filed a complaint with the local industrial and commercial office. The industrial and commercial office took administrative measures against the defendant's specialty store, including temporarily detaining relevant materials and items and ordering the store to refund money to consumers. After mediation failed, Bi Yongzhen filed a lawsuit with the Beiguan District People's Court of Anyang City, Henan Province, requesting that Hou Guangzhou return the purchase price of RMB 2,390 and pay double compensation of RMB 2,390.

(2) Judgment

The court hearing the case held that operators shall provide consumers with true information about the goods and shall not engage in misleading false publicity. Where a consumer's lawful rights and interests are damaged when purchasing goods, the consumer may claim compensation from the seller. In this case, the promotional leaflets distributed by Hou Guangzhou to an unspecified group, including Bi Yongzhen, were sufficient to deceive and mislead consumers and constituted false advertising of goods. The goods provided by Hou Guangzhou to Bi Yongzhen were sold using false advertising, which constituted fraudulent conduct, and for which Hou Guangzhou had been investigated and punished by the industrial and commercial authorities. Accordingly, Hou Guangzhou should compensate Bi Yongzhen for his losses in addition to the amount of the purchase price, with the additional compensation being equal to one times the purchase price of the goods. On December 31, 2010, the court ruled that Hou Guangzhou should return the purchase price of RMB 2,390 to Bi Yongzhen and pay Bi Yongzhen double compensation of RMB 2,390.

Case 7

Liu Zhongyun v. Bank of China Co., Ltd., Hengyang Branch, and China Construction Bank Co., Ltd., Hengyang Branch — Dispute over Property Damage Compensation

— Where a Consumer's UnionPay Card Number and Password Are Copied During a Withdrawal and the Deposits Are Withdrawn, the Bank Providing the UnionPay Card Shall Bear Compensation Liability

(1) Basic Facts

Liu Zhongyun opened a UnionPay card with CCB Hengyang Branch. On January 30, 2009, he went to an ATM at the outlet of CCB Hengyang Branch located on Jiefang Road in Hengyang City to withdraw money but failed. He then went to an ATM at an outlet of BOC Hengyang Branch next door and withdrew RMB 2,500, leaving a deposit balance of RMB 41,395.49 in his account. At the time of withdrawal, the ATM had been illegally fitted with a camera by others, who used the recorded footage to copy the information from Liu Zhongyun's bank card. The next day, Liu Zhongyun's bank card was used to make 10 successive withdrawals at other banks' ATMs, each time RMB 2,000, totaling RMB 20,000, and each withdrawal incurred a service fee of RMB 2, totaling RMB 20 in fees. Finally, a transfer of RMB 21,300 was made via an ATM, with a transfer service fee of RMB 52. Thus, within the same day, Liu Zhongyun's bank card conducted 11 transactions at other banks' ATMs, totaling RMB 41,372 (including fees), leaving a deposit balance of only RMB 23.49. Liu Zhongyun then filed a lawsuit with the Yanfeng District People's Court of Hengyang City, Hunan Province, requesting that BOC Hengyang Branch and CCB Hengyang Branch compensate him for the RMB 41,372 deposit and interest.

(2) Judgment

The court of first instance held BOC Hengyang Branch liable for compensation and exonerated CCB Hengyang Branch. Dissatisfied, BOC Hengyang Branch appealed, requesting that CCB Hengyang Branch bear compensation liability. The Hengyang Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province held in the second instance that Liu Zhongyun opened a UnionPay card with CCB Hengyang Branch, forming a savings deposit contract relationship between the parties. The parties shall adhere to the principle of good faith and perform duties such as notification, assistance, and confidentiality in accordance with the nature, purpose, and trade practices of the contract. CCB Hengyang Branch had the obligation to ensure that the funds in the depositor's bank card were not stolen by others, and also had the obligation to notify and inform the cardholder of the methods and preventive measures criminals use with various high-tech means to steal deposits in bank cards. Since CCB Hengyang Branch, as the issuing bank, could neither ensure the security of the information on the bank cards it issued nor inform the cardholder of the methods criminals use to obtain card information and passwords with high-tech means, it should bear civil liability for the theft of the funds in Liu Zhongyun's bank card. Liu Zhongyun, as an ordinary cardholder, did not understand the structure and working principle of ATMs, nor did he have the ability to identify the devices criminals install on ATMs to steal card information and passwords using high-tech means. Moreover, Liu Zhongyun had not lost his bank card or password, nor had he entrusted others to use them. Therefore, Liu Zhongyun had no fault in the leakage of his bank card information and password and should not bear liability. When Liu Zhongyun withdrew money from the ATM of BOC Hengyang Branch, that bank paid the deposit to Liu Zhongyun based on an agency relationship, performing its obligation to pay deposits on behalf of the principal. According to the General Principles of the Civil Law, an agent, within the scope of agency authority, implements civil juristic acts in the name of the principal, and the principal bears civil liability for the agent's acts. Therefore, CCB Hengyang Branch, as the principal, should bear liability for the agency acts of BOC Hengyang Branch. The court of second instance amended the judgment, ordering CCB Hengyang Branch to pay Liu Zhongyun the savings deposit of RMB 41,372.

Case 8

Sun Baojing v. Shanghai Yidingdei Beauty Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Health Care Service Contract

— "Overlord Clauses" in Health Care Service Contracts Are Invalid, and Prepaid Service Fees for Unconsumed Services Shall Be Refunded

(1) Basic Facts

Case 8

Sun Baojing v. Shanghai Yidingde Beauty Co., Ltd. — dispute over service contract

Basic Facts

On July 18, 2010, Sun Baojing entered into a service agreement with Shanghai Yidingde Beauty Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yidingde Company), stipulating: the service period was six months; Sun Baojing selected the premium course valued at RMB 100,000, and all items were to be deducted from the card at a 15% discount off the unit price. If Sun Baojing failed to receive services in accordance with the plan and schedule, and did not improve after a good-faith reminder and exceeded the service period, she would be deemed to have waived the service; if she could not perform according to the formulated plan due to her own reasons, she could not request a refund of any fees already paid; if she was unable to participate in the relevant programs for three consecutive months due to her own reasons, Yidingde Company had the right to terminate the service, and Sun Baojing could not demand a refund or compensation. Yidingde Company issued a declaration to Sun Baojing, stating that Sun Baojing must comply with the consultant's instructions and arrangements; if the course failed or progressed slowly due to personal reasons, Yidingde Company would not be liable, would not refund the balance, and reserved the right to pursue liability for breach of contract. Sun Baojing signed and confirmed the declaration. Subsequently, Sun Baojing paid a service fee of RMB 100,000 to Yidingde Company in two installments and received multiple weight-loss treatment services. Later, Sun Baojing stopped receiving weight-loss treatments because her weight did not decrease. Sun Baojing filed a lawsuit with the court on the grounds that she had lost confidence in Yidingde Company's services and the service period had expired, and that Yidingde Company had collected service fees but failed to provide effective services, requesting rescission of the service agreement and a refund of RMB 90,000 by Yidingde Company.

Judgment

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance that when Sun Baojing filed the lawsuit, the termination date stipulated in the service agreement had already passed, and the service agreement had become invalid; therefore, Sun Baojing did not need to seek rescission of the agreement. Sun Baojing unilaterally abandoned the services and should bear the consequences arising therefrom. Since Sun Baojing did not accept the full amount of services for the prepaid amount, she was not entitled to the discount for the services she had already received. The total price for the services received was RMB 31,800, which was deducted from the prepayment of RMB 100,000. Although the service agreement and declaration stated that if Sun Baojing abandoned or did not receive services as arranged, no fees would be refunded, these terms were standard-form clauses provided by Yidingde Company. They did not follow the principle of fairness in defining the rights and obligations between the parties, and clearly increased Sun Baojing's liability while excluding her rights; therefore, such clauses were invalid. The court comprehensively considered factors such as the degree of performance of the agreement, the circumstances of service provision, and the degree of fault of Sun Baojing in unilaterally abandoning the services, and determined, in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith, that Sun Baojing should pay Yidingde Company RMB 20,000 as liquidated damages. After deducting the service fee of RMB 31,800 and the liquidated damages of RMB 20,000 from the prepayment of RMB 100,000, Yidingde Company still needed to refund Sun Baojing RMB 48,200. Accordingly, the court of second instance ruled that Yidingde Company should refund Sun Baojing RMB 48,200 in a lump sum and dismissed Sun Baojing's other claims.

Case 9

Chen Xi v. Chongqing Far East Department Store Co., Ltd. — dispute over product quality

—— Where the quality grade indicated on the packaging of sold food is false, the seller shall bear the liability of refund and compensation at one times the price

Basic Facts

On December 1, 2012, Chen Xi purchased from Chongqing Far East Department Store Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Far East Department Store) a total of 21 bottles of the following products: HuiMouTang Loquat Honey with a production date of September 26, 2012; HuiMouTang Acacia Honey with a production date of October 11, 2012; WeiDuoli Jujube Flower Honey with a production date of July 9, 2012; WeiDuoli Wolfberry Honey with a production date of July 10, 2012; and WeiDuoli Acacia Honey with a production date of July 20, 2012. The total price was RMB 873.3. The outer packaging labels of these products indicated the quality grade as Grade One, and the food safety standards complied with GB14963. However, the "National Food Safety Standard Honey" (GB14963-2011) issued by the Ministry of Health did not include a Grade One classification, and this standard came into effect on October 20, 2011. Chen Xi filed a lawsuit with the Jiangbei District People's Court of Chongqing, requesting a return of the goods, a full refund of the purchase price from Far East Department Store, and compensation equal to one times the purchase price.

Judgment

The court of first instance held after trial that the honey sold by Far East Department Store had labels indicating the product quality as Grade One, and its food safety implementation standard was the "National Food Safety Standard Honey" (GB14963-2011) issued by the Ministry of Health, which did not contain a Grade One level. Therefore, the goods in dispute were products with non-compliant labels. Article 23 of the Product Quality Law provides that a seller shall establish and implement a system of inspection and acceptance of purchased goods, and shall verify the product certificate and other markings. Far East Department Store, as the seller of the goods, had the obligation to verify whether the "product quality as Grade One" indicated on the goods sold in its store complied with the food safety standards. Because it failed to fulfill its strict examination obligations and sold goods with false markings, it misled consumers into making untrue expressions of intent, and its conduct constituted fraud. Where an operator provides goods or services with fraudulent conduct, it shall, at the request of the consumer, increase compensation for the losses suffered by the consumer, with the amount of increased compensation being one times the price of the goods purchased by the consumer. Therefore, Chen Xi's claims for return of the goods and compensation at one times the purchase price were supported. The court of first instance ruled that Far East Department Store should refund Chen Xi the purchase price of RMB 873.3 and pay compensation of RMB 873.3, totaling RMB 1,746.6. Far East Department Store appealed against the judgment of first instance, and the court of second instance affirmed the original judgment.

Case 10

Teng Shuang v. Nanjing Chengji Education Information Consulting Co., Ltd. — dispute over education service contract

—— Where the operator breaches the contract, the consumer's claim for a partial refund of service fees shall be supported in accordance with law

Basic Facts

On July 4, 2009, Teng Shuang entered into a registration agreement for tutoring classes with Nanjing Chengji Education Information Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chengji Company), stipulating that Teng Shuang paid RMB 6,020 to order a "two-year high-grade Peking University Affiliated High School (Affiliated Primary School) online school with a free low-grade online school learning." The remarks column of the agreement stated: "Summer vacation, winter vacation, Saturday, Sunday tutoring: Grade 8 + Grade 7 with a free Grade 6 (including all tutoring for three years)," and the tutoring location was at Shanxi Road, Nanjing. After the agreement was signed, Teng Shuang paid the online school tutoring fee of RMB 6,020 to Chengji Company as agreed. In mid-October 2009, Chengji Company moved its operations to a distant location, and the tutoring classes at the contractually agreed location ceased accordingly. Because Chengji Company failed to provide education services as agreed, Teng Shuang filed a lawsuit with the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province on June 4, 2010, requesting that Chengji Company refund the tutoring fee of RMB 5,000.

Judgment

The court of first instance held after trial that Chengji Company, by providing education goods and services to Teng Shuang on a prepayment basis, was obligated to provide Teng Shuang with an online school learning card and tutoring classes at the Shanxi Road, Nanjing registration point during summer and winter vacations, Saturdays, and Sundays, in accordance with the registration agreement. Now, due to its own business reasons, Chengji Company could not continue to provide Teng Shuang with tutoring classes at the Shanxi Road, Nanjing registration point as agreed in the contract. Therefore, Teng Shuang's request for a refund of the corresponding prepayment was in accordance with the law. In this case, Teng Shuang prepaid RMB 6,020 as tutoring fees, which included three years of online school learning card fees and three years of tutoring class fees. The tutoring classes had only been running for about three months when they ceased. Therefore, Teng Shuang's request that Chengji Company refund the prepaid tutoring fee of RMB 5,000 for the remaining period was supported. The court ruled that Chengji Company should refund Teng Shuang the prepaid tutoring fee of RMB 5,000. Chengji Company appealed against the judgment of first instance to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court. The court of second instance affirmed the original judgment.
